messages.subject: Running time error
parts:
,Hi
:I'm attempting to compute MSE of parameters for my simulated data, based on gamma-count, Poisson and nbinomial distributions. But after some repetitions (at most 8th repetition), I got this error


file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 755a4114e167 date: Wed Aug 19 15:24:56 2015 +0200
Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 829, Thread: 0
 ... Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it


gsl: gamma_inc.c:181: ERROR: error in large x asymptotic
.Default GSL error handler invoked
:() Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed 
.The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully
.If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org<
:In addition: Warning message
running command '"C:/Users/Mahsa Nadifar/Documents/R/win-library/3.2/INLA/bin/windows/inla32.exe" -b -s -v "C:/Users/MAHSAN~1/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAVrJ4f/file68688552a3c29/Model.ini"' had status 3 


.What does it mean? I'm running R 3.2.3 on Windows


:my code




simfun <- function(m, n.i, usd, esd, b) {
ntot <- m*n.i
u <- rnorm(m, sd = usd)
eps <- rnorm(ntot, sd = esd)
x1 <- rnorm(ntot, 0, 2) 
x2 <- rnorm(ntot, 0, 2) 
dd <- data.frame(cbind(x1,x2), f = factor(rep(1:m, each = n.i)))
dd$eta0 <- cbind(x1,x2)%*% b
dd$eta <- with(dd, eta0 + u[f] + eps)
nu <- rgamma(ntot, 5, 1)
dd$mu <- nu*exp(dd$eta)
dd$ID <- rep(1:n.i, m)
dd$y <- with(dd, rpois(ntot, lambda = mu))
dd
}




### Information 
m <- 20 #the number of areas
n.i <- 6 #the number of area's population
usd <- 2 #the value of u's sd
esd <- 1 #the value of epsilon's sd
b=coef <- c(0.2, 0.8) #regression coefficients
alpha <- 0.5 #the value of dispersed parameter



#### MSE


                      R <- 30                          #the number of repition for computing MSE
k <- 10                          #the number of clones


##################
BETA.hat.GC <- BETA.hat.P <- BETA.hat.NB <- matrix( , ncol=2, nrow=R)




ALPHA.hat.mean <- ALPHA.hat.sd <- logscore.GC <- logscore.P <- logscore.NB <- c()
DIC.GC <- DIC.P <- DIC.NB <- c()
ALPHA.hat.con.int <- matrix( , ncol=2, nrow=R)


for(r in 1:R){
###
dd <- simfun(m=m, n.i=n.i, usd=usd, esd=esd, b=coef)
"y.k" <- rep(dd$y,k)
"x1.k" <- rep(dd$x1,k)
"x2.k" <- rep(dd$x2,k)
"f.k" <- rep(1:(m*k),each=n.i)
"ID.k" <- rep(dd$ID,k)
clone.data <- as.data.frame(cbind(x1.k,x2.k,f.k,ID.k,y.k))




### INLA.Result
formula.k <- y.k ~ -1 + x1.k + x2.k + f(f.k, model="iid") + f(ID.k, model="iid")


result1.clone <- inla(formula.k, family = c("gammacount"), data = clone.data, 
control.compute = list(dic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)
result2.clone <- inla(formula.k, family = c( "poisson"), data = clone.data, 
control.compute = list(dic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)
result3.clone <- inla(formula.k, family = c("nbinomial"), data = clone.data, 
control.compute = list(dic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)


### Coef.hat.mean
BETA.hat.GC[r,] <- result1.clone$summary.fixed[,1]
BETA.hat.P[r,] <- result2.clone$summary.fixed[,1]
BETA.hat.NB[r,] <- result3.clone$summary.fixed[,1]




### Alpha.hat
# Mean
ALPHA.hat.mean[r] <- result1.clone$summary.hyper[1,1]




### DIC
DIC.GC[r] <- result1.clone$dic$dic
DIC.P[r] <- result2.clone$dic$dic
DIC.NB[r] <- result3.clone$dic$dic


print(c(r,date()))
}

On Sat, 2016-07-30 at 03:27 -0700, mahsa nadifar wrote:
>
>
>
> ,Hi
> :I'm attempting to compute MSE of parameters for my simulated data,
> based on gamma-count, Poisson and nbinomial distributions. But after
> some repetitions (at most 8th repetition), I got this error
>

the main issue is that the experiemnt is badly designed giving also
extreme counts. 

the gammacount likelihood is computed as log(CDF(y+1..,)-CDF(y...,))
 and this might fail for high counts like yours. 

you see this also for all the NAN/INF warnings you get in the output.

although its possible to replace the above with an asymptotic expansion
for large y, which goes like -n*y*a/b + constant(a,b), your problem
will remain.

see if you can set the simulation values so that somewhat more
reasonable values for dd$y are obtained.
